title: Authentication settings: turning off email and password with no other sign-in method saves without warning, and everyone is locked out
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

From a real-user walkthrough of Setup, filed on the maintainer's word: 「以上都同意，立卡」 (2026-11-05). Measured on `main` `b7075d9908`, with the console in dev mode, unless a line says otherwise. Test app scaffolded with `create-objectstack@18.3.0`.

## What a customer sees

An administrator plans to move to single sign-on and turns off 启用邮箱/密码登录 before SSO is configured. It saves. As soon as people sign out, no one can sign back in, the administrator included, and the fix needs an environment variable or a database edit.

## Measured

- Setup → Settings → Authentication, switch off, 保存更改: toast 「设置已保存」, no warning or confirmation. `socialProviders` is empty and SSO is off.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`: 400 `EMAIL_PASSWORD_DISABLED`.
- `GET /api/v1/auth/config`: `emailPassword.enabled: false`.
- The login page still drew the email and password form, and submitting showed `Email and password is not enabled`, in English. #29159 changed this page's copy for the same state and is closed; this was read under `os dev` through the console dev server, so the dev sign-in affordance may have influenced what was drawn.

## Expected

The save is refused while it would leave no sign-in method, and names what to configure first. When email and password really are off, the login page does not offer the form.
